title: Investigating Intersectional Bias in Large Language Models using Confidence Disparities in Coreference Resolution

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity (differences in model uncertainty) on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with age-related demographic markers (young, old) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with body type demographic markers (thin, fat) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with disability markers (neurotypical, able-bodied, neurodivergent, disabled) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with gender identity markers (cisgender, transgender) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with language markers (English-speaking, non-English-speaking) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with nationality markers (American, immigrant) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with sexual orientation markers (heterosexual, gay) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with socio-economic status markers (rich, poor) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with race markers (White, Black, Asian, Hispanic) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating Coreference Confidence Disparity on a coreference resolution task when occupational referents are augmented with religion markers (Christian, Muslim, Jewish) intersected with binary gender pronouns.

Evaluating differences in coreference resolution confidence when using masculine versus feminine pronouns, establishing the base axis of intersectionality across all other evaluated demographic markers.
